questions.stem: A newborn girl becomes cyanotic on her first day of life. Oxygen saturation is 80% on room air. There is a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that becomes louder with inspiration. Chest x-ray shows a very large, box-shaped heart. ECG shows a short PR interval and a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex. Echocardiography shows the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve attached low in the right ventricle, with a very large right atrium and right-to-left flow across the atrial septum. Her mother most likely needed long-term drug treatment during pregnancy for which condition?
choices: Epilepsy
Severe nodular acne
Bipolar I disorder
Graves disease
Mechanical heart valve
questions.explanation: This is **Ebstein anomaly**: the tricuspid leaflets sit low in the right ventricle, causing **tricuspid regurgitation**, a huge right atrium and right-to-left flow across the atrial septum. The ECG shows **pre-excitation (WPW)**, a classic association. **Ebstein anomaly** is linked to maternal **lithium**, the main long-term drug for **bipolar disorder**. Isotretinoin for acne is a strong teratogen, but its heart defects are mainly **conotruncal** (outflow tract) defects, not downward displacement of the tricuspid valve.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **anomalia de Ebstein**: os folhetos da tricúspide ficam implantados mais abaixo (deslocados em direção ao ápice) no ventrículo direito, causando **insuficiência tricúspide**, um átrio direito enorme e fluxo direita-esquerda pelo septo interatrial. O ECG mostra **pré-excitação (WPW)**, uma associação clássica. A anomalia de Ebstein está ligada ao uso materno de **lítio**, o principal fármaco de uso prolongado no **transtorno bipolar**. A isotretinoína usada para acne é um teratógeno potente, mas seus defeitos cardíacos são principalmente **conotruncais** (da via de saída), e não o deslocamento da valva tricúspide para baixo.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy is evaluated for headaches. Blood pressure is 166/94 mm Hg in the right arm, 164/92 mm Hg in the left arm, and 112/74 mm Hg in the right leg. Femoral pulses are weak and arrive later than the radial pulses. An early systolic click is heard at the apex. Chest x-ray shows small notches on the lower borders of several middle ribs on both sides. Which mechanism best explains the rib finding?
choices: Bone resorption caused by secondary hyperparathyroidism
Pressure from an aneurysm of the ascending aorta
Erosion by large intercostal veins that drain a blocked vena cava
Marrow expansion caused by chronic hypoxemia and polycythemia
Erosion by large intercostal arteries that bypass a narrowing
questions.explanation: This is **coarctation of the aorta** beyond the left subclavian artery: arm pressures are high, leg pressures are low, and femoral pulses are weak and delayed; the click suggests an associated **bicuspid aortic valve**. Blood bypasses the narrowing through the internal thoracic arteries into the **intercostal arteries**, which flow backward into the descending aorta. These vessels enlarge and **erode the lower rib borders** (rib notching). Dilated intercostal veins can appear with vena cava obstruction, but they do not explain the arm-leg pressure gap or the weak femoral pulses.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **coarctação da aorta** distal à artéria subclávia esquerda: a pressão é alta nos braços e baixa nas pernas, e os pulsos femorais são fracos e atrasados; o clique sugere uma **valva aórtica bicúspide** associada. O sangue contorna o estreitamento pelas artérias torácicas internas até as **artérias intercostais**, que fluem de forma retrógrada para a aorta descendente. Esses vasos se dilatam e **erodem a borda inferior das costelas** (erosões costais, *rib notching*). Veias intercostais dilatadas podem surgir na obstrução da veia cava, mas não explicam a diferença de pressão entre braços e pernas nem os pulsos femorais fracos.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has had sharp chest pain for 2 days. He had a cold 1 week ago. The pain is worse when he lies flat and better when he sits up and leans forward. He also feels pain along the top of his left shoulder, over the trapezius ridge. A scratchy, three-part sound is heard at the left sternal border. ECG shows diffuse ST elevation with PR depression. Pain fibers in which nerve explain the pain over the trapezius ridge?
choices: Vagus nerve
Phrenic nerve
Spinal accessory nerve
Greater splanchnic nerve
Intercostal nerves
questions.explanation: This is **acute pericarditis**. Pain from the **fibrous and parietal pericardium** travels in the **phrenic nerve** (C3-C5), so the pain is felt in skin from the same spinal segments: the shoulder and **trapezius ridge**. The spinal accessory nerve gives motor supply to the trapezius muscle but carries no pain fibers from the pericardium. The visceral pericardium itself is largely insensitive to pain.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **pericardite aguda**. A dor do **pericárdio fibroso e do folheto parietal** segue pelo **nervo frênico** (C3-C5); por isso a dor é sentida na pele dos mesmos segmentos espinhais: o ombro e a **borda do trapézio**. O nervo acessório dá a inervação motora do músculo trapézio, mas não conduz fibras de dor do pericárdio. O pericárdio visceral em si é praticamente insensível à dor.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man has had severe chest pain for 2 hours. ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads V1 to V4 and a new right bundle branch block. One hour later, his vital signs are: pulse 44/min, blood pressure 94/60 mm Hg, respiratory rate 20/min. The ECG now shows a constant PR interval, and some P waves are suddenly not followed by a QRS complex. The QRS complexes are wide. Branches of which artery supply the conduction tissue most likely damaged in this patient?
choices: Right coronary artery, through the AV nodal artery
Right coronary artery, through the SA nodal artery
Left circumflex artery, through obtuse marginal branches
Left anterior descending artery, through septal branches
Right coronary artery, through acute marginal branches
questions.explanation: ST elevation in V1 to V4 means an **anterior infarction** from the **LAD**. A new bundle branch block plus **Mobitz II** block with wide QRS complexes means damage **below the AV node**, in the His bundle and bundle branches. These run in the anterior two-thirds of the septum, which the **septal branches of the LAD** supply. The AV nodal artery, usually from the RCA, explains the AV nodal block seen in inferior infarction, which is typically Mobitz I with narrow QRS complexes.
questions.explanation_pt: Supradesnivelamento do ST de V1 a V4 indica **infarto anterior** por oclusão da **DA**. Um bloqueio de ramo novo associado a **bloqueio AV de 2º grau Mobitz II** com QRS largo indica lesão **abaixo do nó AV**, no feixe de His e nos ramos. Eles passam pelos dois terços anteriores do septo, irrigados pelos **ramos septais da DA**. A artéria do nó AV, geralmente originada da CD, explica o bloqueio nodal do infarto inferior, que tipicamente é Mobitz I com QRS estreito.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man suddenly cannot see the left side of objects with either eye. Brain imaging shows a small acute infarct in the right occipital lobe. His heart sounds are normal, and the ECG shows sinus rhythm. Carotid ultrasound is normal. During echocardiography, agitated saline is injected into an arm vein. At rest, no bubbles reach the left heart. When he releases a Valsalva maneuver, bubbles appear in the left atrium within 3 heartbeats. Which change allows the bubbles to cross?
choices: Right atrial pressure briefly rising above left atrial pressure
Left atrial pressure briefly rising above right atrial pressure
Pulmonary vascular resistance permanently rising above systemic resistance
Bubbles passing through dilated pulmonary capillaries
Blood flowing from the pulmonary artery to the aorta
questions.explanation: This is a **patent foramen ovale**: the septum primum lies against the septum secundum but never fused with it. Normally **left atrial pressure** is higher and keeps this flap closed. When the Valsalva is released, venous blood rushes back to the right heart, **right atrial pressure** rises above left, the flap opens, and blood (or a clot) crosses right to left. Bubbles passing through the lung, as in pulmonary arteriovenous shunts, usually appear later, after several heartbeats, and do not depend on the Valsalva maneuver.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **forame oval patente (FOP)**: o septum primum fica encostado no septum secundum, mas nunca se fundiu a ele. Normalmente a **pressão do átrio esquerdo** é maior e mantém essa válvula fechada. Ao soltar a manobra de Valsalva, o sangue venoso retorna rapidamente ao coração direito, a **pressão do átrio direito** supera a do esquerdo, a válvula se abre e o sangue (ou um trombo) passa da direita para a esquerda. Microbolhas que atravessam o pulmão, como nas fístulas arteriovenosas pulmonares, costumam aparecer mais tarde, após vários batimentos, e não dependem da manobra de Valsalva.

questions.stem: A 2-month-old girl with upslanting palpebral fissures, a single palmar crease, and low muscle tone is brought in because she sweats and breathes fast during feeds. She has gained little weight. Echocardiography shows one common atrioventricular valve, a defect in the lowest part of the atrial septum, and a defect in the inlet part of the ventricular septum. Failure of which embryologic process best explains her heart defect?
choices: Migration of neural crest cells into the outflow tract
Fusion of the septum primum with the septum secundum
Growth of the muscular ventricular septum
Fusion of the endocardial cushions
Spiral rotation of the aorticopulmonary septum
questions.explanation: This girl has **Down syndrome** and a complete **atrioventricular septal defect**. The **endocardial cushions** form the center of the heart: the lowest part of the atrial septum, the inlet ventricular septum, and the mitral and tricuspid valves. When they do not fuse, the result is an ostium primum defect, an inlet VSD, and one common AV valve. Failure of the septum primum to fuse with the septum secundum leaves a **patent foramen ovale**, which lies in the middle of the atrial septum and does not involve the AV valves.
questions.explanation_pt: A menina tem **síndrome de Down** e um **defeito do septo atrioventricular (DSAV)** total. Os **coxins endocárdicos** formam o centro do coração: a parte mais baixa do septo interatrial, o septo interventricular de entrada e as valvas mitral e tricúspide. Quando eles não se fundem, surgem uma CIA tipo ostium primum, uma CIV de via de entrada e uma valva AV única. A falta de fusão do septum primum com o septum secundum deixa um **forame oval patente**, que fica no meio do septo interatrial e não envolve as valvas AV.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman has had worsening shortness of breath on exertion for 1 year. As a child she had a loud heart murmur from a ventricular septal defect, but she never had surgery. Now she has clubbing of the fingers and toes and bluish lips. Oxygen saturation is 82% on room air, hemoglobin is 20.4 g/dL, and hematocrit is 61%. The second heart sound has a loud pulmonic component. The old loud murmur is now soft. Which change best explains her cyanosis?
choices: Spontaneous closure of the ventricular septal defect
Muscle thickening that narrows the right ventricular outflow tract
Pulmonary arteriole remodeling that raises right-sided pressures
Left ventricular failure that fills the alveoli with fluid
New arteriovenous malformations inside the lungs
questions.explanation: This is **Eisenmenger syndrome**. Years of high flow through the left-to-right shunt cause **intimal and medial thickening of the pulmonary arterioles**. Pulmonary vascular resistance rises until right-sided pressure is higher than left, and the shunt **reverses** to right-to-left, causing late cyanosis, clubbing and secondary polycythemia. The murmur is softer because the pressures on both sides are now close, and the **loud P2** shows pulmonary hypertension; narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract would make P2 soft, and a closed VSD would not cause cyanosis.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **síndrome de Eisenmenger**. Anos de hiperfluxo pelo shunt esquerda-direita causam **espessamento da íntima e da média das arteríolas pulmonares**. A resistência vascular pulmonar aumenta até a pressão do lado direito superar a do esquerdo, e o shunt se **inverte** para direita-esquerda, causando cianose tardia, baqueteamento digital e policitemia secundária. O sopro fica mais suave porque as pressões dos dois lados agora estão próximas, e a **P2 hiperfonética** indica hipertensão pulmonar; o estreitamento da via de saída do ventrículo direito tornaria a P2 hipofonética, e uma CIV fechada não causaria cianose.

questions.stem: A 4-day-old boy has a seizure. He has been mildly cyanotic since birth. He has a small jaw and low-set ears. Laboratory studies show serum calcium 6.4 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5) and a low parathyroid hormone level. Chest x-ray shows no thymic shadow. Echocardiography shows a single large artery leaving the heart above a ventricular septal defect; the coronary, pulmonary and systemic arteries all branch from it. Which genetic finding is most likely?
choices: Trisomy 21
Microdeletion at 22q11.2
Monosomy X (45,X)
Microdeletion at 7q11.23
Trisomy 18
questions.explanation: This is **22q11.2 deletion syndrome** (DiGeorge): abnormal development of the **third and fourth pharyngeal pouches** gives no thymus and no parathyroids, so **hypocalcemia** with low PTH, while abnormal **neural crest** migration gives a **conotruncal defect**, here **persistent truncus arteriosus**. The 7q11.23 deletion (Williams syndrome) also affects the heart, but it causes **supravalvular aortic stenosis** and **high** calcium, not low calcium.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **síndrome da deleção 22q11.2** (DiGeorge): o desenvolvimento anormal da **terceira e quarta bolsas faríngeas** leva à ausência de timo e de paratireoides, portanto **hipocalcemia** com PTH baixo, enquanto a migração anormal da **crista neural** leva a um **defeito conotruncal**, aqui o **tronco arterial comum** (*truncus arteriosus*). A deleção 7q11.23 (síndrome de Williams) também afeta o coração, mas causa **estenose aórtica supravalvar** e cálcio **alto**, e não baixo.
